validation_holdout_split.description: Disjoint 50/50 partition of the 42,721 validation transactions into calibrator fitting and evaluation subsets.
validation_holdout_split.observation_reuse: Zero observation reuse: fitting and evaluation sets are strictly disjoint indices.

calibration_methodology.fitting_procedure: Isotonic Regression (sklearn.isotonic.IsotonicRegression with out_of_bounds='clip') fitted exclusively on the 21,360 fitting rows mapping raw model probabilities to binary labels y_cal.
calibration_methodology.evaluation_procedure: Calibrator evaluated exclusively on the held-out 21,361 evaluation rows (p_eval, y_eval).
calibration_methodology.brier_score_formula: Brier Score = (1 / N) * sum((p_i - y_i)^2), measuring the mean squared error between predicted probabilities and actual binary outcomes. Lower is better. Baseline naive brier = base_rate * (1 - base_rate) = 0.00173.
calibration_methodology.distortion_source_and_strategy: CatBoost trained with auto_class_weights='Balanced' artificially shifts output scores upwards (mean predicted 0.0032 vs base rate 0.00173). Direct empirical threshold search on raw scores (0.144) bypasses distortion because monotonicity is preserved. Post-hoc isotonic calibration provides calibrated probabilities (reducing Brier score by 28.1%) for downstream interpretability without altering ranking.

calibration_observations: 1. CatBoost was trained with auto_class_weights='Balanced', which shifts uncalibrated output probabilities upward (mean = 0.0032 vs base rate 0.00173). This causes its empirical optimal threshold under S2 (0.144) to differ from the theoretical Bayes threshold (~0.0099). 2. LightGBM (scale_pos_weight=5.0) yields an empirical optimal threshold of 0.006. 3. Isotonic calibration on a 50% validation holdout reduces Brier score significantly (CatBoost: 0.000759 -> 0.000546, a 28.1% improvement). 4. Empirical threshold search directly on the uncalibrated probabilities remains robust, bypassing probability distortion while preserving ranking order.
